texts.li: {GIVER} of {FACTION} has sent word that {COUNT} {KIND} strayed from their herd and are now on the colony's land. {GIVER} asks the colony to keep them safe until the herders come for them.

[ws:drove] With every herd in the region on the drove roads this season, {COUNT} {KIND} of {FACTION}'s strayed from the road and are now on the colony's land. {GIVER} asks the colony to keep them safe until the herders come for them.

[ws:herds] With {WSNAME} on the move, every herd in the region is restless, and {COUNT} {KIND} of {FACTION}'s broke away and are now on the colony's land. {GIVER} asks the colony to keep them safe until the herders come for them.

[wsdef:Council_WS_Murrain] {FACTION} are moving their healthy animals away from {WSNAME}, and {COUNT} {KIND} strayed on the way and are now on the colony's land. {GIVER} asks the colony to keep them safe until the herders come for them.

li.label: Keep them for {FACTION}
li.outcome: The strayed animals are the colony's to look after until the herders come.

li.label: Decline
li.outcome: The strayed animals will wander off.

lines.li: [penned] They are all here and penned, thank you.
[most] Most of them are here, and that will do.
[lost] Half of them are gone, which is a poor return.

terms.li: If the colony agrees, the {KIND} count as the colony's animals until the herders come in {DAYS}, and its handlers can rope them into a pen. {KIND} left outside a pen may wander off the map, and predators may take them.\n\nWhen the herders come, they count the {KIND} and lead them home. If all of them are in a pen or a barn, {FACTION} will be grateful. If half or more are still here, {FACTION} will be satisfied. If fewer are left, {FACTION} will hold it against the colony. If the colony declines, the {KIND} wander off.

accepted.li: The strayed {KIND} are the colony's to look after until {FACTION}'s herders come. Rope them into a pen.

notes.li: [herders] {FACTION}'s herders have come to the gate for their {KIND}.

ends.li: [penned] {FACTION}'s herders found all {COUNT} of their {KIND} in a pen and led them home. {FACTION} are grateful.
[most] {FACTION}'s herders found {SILVER} of their {COUNT} {KIND} in a pen, and led home the ones that were still here.

[lost] {FACTION}'s herders found fewer than half of their {KIND}. The rest, {ITEM}, were taken by predators or wandered off. They led home the ones that were left, and they hold it against the colony.

titles.li: [winter] Keep part of the herd over the winter
[!winter] Keep part of the herd for a season

texts.li: [winter] A few days ago {FACTION}'s herders took their strayed {KIND} home from the colony. There is little grazing on their winter land this year, so {GIVER} asks the colony to keep {COUNT} of the herd over the winter.

[!winter] A few days ago {FACTION}'s herders took their strayed {KIND} home from the colony. There is little grazing on their land this season, so {GIVER} asks the colony to keep {COUNT} of the herd until it grows back.

li.label: Keep them
li.outcome: The herders will bring the animals.

terms.li: [winter] If the colony agrees, the herders bring {COUNT} {KIND} onto the colony's land. They are the colony's to pen and feed until spring, in {DAYS}: by grazing, hay or kibble. The quest shows the hay and kibble in the stores against what they will eat.\n\nIn spring the herders come back for them. If every one is alive, {FACTION} will be grateful. If some die, {FACTION} will ask to be paid for them.

[!winter] If the colony agrees, the herders bring {COUNT} {KIND} onto the colony's land. They are the colony's to pen and feed for {DAYS}: by grazing, hay or kibble. The quest shows the hay and kibble in the stores against what they will eat.\n\nThen the herders come back for them. If every one is alive, {FACTION} will be grateful. If some die, {FACTION} will ask to be paid for them.

accepted.li: The herders of {FACTION} have brought {COUNT} {KIND} onto the colony's land. Pen them and keep them fed.

notes.li: [short] There may not be enough hay or kibble in the stores to feed {FACTION}'s {KIND} until the end of the keeping.

ends.li: [kept,winter] Winter is over, and all of {FACTION}'s {KIND} are alive and well. The herders will come for them soon.
[kept,!winter] The keeping is over, and all of {FACTION}'s {KIND} are alive and well. The herders will come for them soon.
[somedied] {FACTION} lost {ITEM} while the colony kept their herd. The herders will come for the rest soon.

texts.li: [winter,!died] When the herders left {COUNT} {KIND} with the colony, they asked it to keep them until spring. Spring has come, and {GIVER} is coming with the herders to take them home.
[!winter,!died] When the herders left {COUNT} {KIND} with the colony, they asked it to keep them for a season. The season is over, and {GIVER} is coming with the herders to take them home.
[winter,died] When the herders left their {KIND} with the colony, they asked it to keep them until spring. Some of them died. Now {GIVER} is coming with the herders to take the rest home.
[!winter,died] When the herders left their {KIND} with the colony, they asked it to keep them for a season. Some of them died. Now {GIVER} is coming with the herders to take the rest home.

li.label: Hand the animals back
li.outcome: The herders are on their way.

li.label: Not now
li.outcome: The herders will come for their animals anyway.

lines.li: [young] They all came through, and these young ones are yours.
[ask] Some of them died, so we need to talk about what is owed.
[bought] They are yours now, look after them.
[unpaid] Then we will take the rest and go.

terms.li: [!died] If the colony agrees, the herders come within a day and lead their {KIND} home. To thank the colony, they leave young animals of their herd with it.\n\nIf the colony does not answer, they come for their {KIND} anyway and leave nothing.

[died] If the colony agrees, the herders come within a day. They will ask the colony to pay {SILVER} silver for the {KIND} that died. Or the colony can buy the ones that are left for what they are worth, and keep them.\n\nIf the colony does not answer, they come for their {KIND} anyway.

accepted.li: {FACTION}'s herders are on their way for their {KIND}.

notes.li: [came] {FACTION}'s herders have come to the gate for their {KIND}.
[young] {FACTION}'s herders left {ITEM} with the colony. They belong to the colony now.

endTitles.li: [paid] The dead animals are paid for

ends.li: [young,!noyoung] {FACTION}'s herders led their {KIND} home and left {ITEM} with the colony to thank it.
[young,noyoung] {FACTION}'s herders led their {KIND} home and thanked the colony for keeping them.
[paid] The colony paid {FACTION} {SILVER} silver for the {KIND} that died, and the herders led the rest home.
[bought] The colony paid {FACTION} {SILVER} silver for {ITEM}, which stay with the colony. The herders have gone home.
[unpaid] The colony would not pay for the {KIND} that died. {FACTION}'s herders led the rest home, and they hold it against the colony.

texts.li: {GIVER} of {FACTION} has counted the {KIND} the colony kept for them, and some of them died. {GIVER} asks the colony to pay {SILVER} silver for the ones that died. Or the colony can buy the ones that are left for {COUNT} silver, and keep them.\n\nIf the colony refuses, the herders take the rest home and hold it against the colony.

li.label: Pay for the dead animals
li.outcome: The silver is being carried out to {X_nameDef}.

li.label: Buy the ones that are left
li.outcome: The silver is being carried out to {X_nameDef}, and the animals stay with the colony.

li.label: Refuse
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} will take the rest of the herd home.
